question: An otherwise eligible family moves permanently from another Canadian province to Alberta on May 18, registers promptly for AHCIP, and has no special exemption. When does Alberta coverage ordinarily start, and what should the family do during the waiting period?
generated_answer:
According to the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan (AHCIP) rules, when an otherwise eligible family moves permanently to Alberta from another Canadian province, they are subject to a waiting period before their Alberta coverage starts.

The waiting period is typically 3 months from the date of arrival in Alberta. Since the family arrived on May 18, their waiting period would end on August 17.

Ordinarily, Alberta coverage would start on August 18, which is the first day of the month following the end of the waiting period.

During the waiting period, the family should maintain their out-of-province health insurance coverage, if they have it, or purchase private health insurance to cover any medical expenses incurred during this time. They should also keep receipts for any medical expenses incurred during the waiting period, as they may be eligible for reimbursement once their Alberta coverage starts.

It's essential for the family to register promptly for AHCIP, as they have done, to ensure they receive their Alberta health care card and coverage as soon as possible after the waiting period ends.
